findings.scenario: Negative cases 4-7 mutate stored record fields, but any field mutation also breaks the canonical self-hash, so every such fixture can collapse into the case-17 authorization-hash-mismatch rejection and the targeted guard is never individually exercised against a hash-consistent forged record.
findings.remediation: State that each mutated negative copy recomputes /authorizationHash/digest so the targeted guard, not the self-hash check, produces the rejection; reserve case 17 for the hash-mismatch proof.

findings.scenario: Case 18 requires the verifier-driven negative suite to prove rejection of an extra write outside the exact goal write set, but the verifier reads only three exact receipt paths and no inventory/census mechanism is specified, so an inert extra file may be undetectable by verify-plan-authority alone.
findings.remediation: Name the mechanism that proves case 18: a pinned write-set inventory in the verifier or the diff/source-census gate with its own fixture.

findings.scenario: The receipt fail-closed sentence pins only enumerated top-level keys, unlike the registry-record contract which fails closed at every object level; an extra nested key could survive schema validation and rely only on pinned-value checks.
findings.remediation: Append 'at every object level' to the receipt fail-closed sentence.
